# Section A

Workpaper WP-015
1) Inspection of batch certificates for lot 2024-CT-118 showed the "ASTM F963-23" conformance field printed with a date later than the shipment date; the exception remains open because no independent test report is attached to the certificate.
2) Review of the age-marking artwork PDF (rev. 3) on the production server revealed that the "3+" warning block was replaced with a "6+" block; the open exception is the missing change-control ticket authorizing that label revision.
3) Reconciliation of the lab file LSP-7741 against the vendor invoice showed the test fee paid corresponds to a different product SKU than the one named in the report; the exception stays open pending confirmation from the vendor which SKU was actually tested.
4) Sampling of 40 units from finished-goods bin FG-22 produced 9 units whose battery compartments required a tool to open, contrary to the "tool-free" statement in the compliance matrix row 14; the open item is the absence of a documented nonconformance report for that bin.
5) Examination of the export declaration EX-0917 listed the HS code for age-verified educational toys rather than general plastic toys; the unresolved exception is the mismatch between that code and the declared contents field on the same document.

# Section B

Counts CT-020
1) The batch of 2,400 units was staged in warehouse dock 4 on 14 March; the staging log entry STG-118 proves it, but the required quality-hold release signature is missing from the log.
2) A container booking for the failed lot was confirmed by freight forwarder FV-Global on 15 March; the booking reference FV-88231 proves it, but the internal pre-shipment clearance code that should precede the booking is missing.
3) The revised "6+" warning label was printed at 6,000 copies on 12 March per press run record PR-0441; that record proves it, but the sign-off from the regulatory affairs field on the label approval form is missing.
4) The lab file for lot 2024-CT-118 was moved from the "pending" folder to the "approved" folder on the compliance server on 13 March, shown by the file-system audit trail entry FT-2290; the reviewer's second-level verification stamp that the approval policy requires is missing.
5) The customer-facing product page for the toy was updated to remove the choking-hazard notice on 16 March, confirmed by the CMS revision history entry RH-3312; the missing verification mark is the legal-compliance review flag that the page-change workflow logs when a safety notice is edited.
